title: Mouthing It at the Back
genre: Scottish ceilidh folk-rock (accordion and fiddle with a full rock backline, Waterboys and Runrig lineage)
subject: a minister's speechwriter stands at the back of the hall mouthing every line, then the minister drops her best pun, and she mouths the rest into the silence
caption: Scottish ceilidh folk-rock, driving and brisk. Accordion playing bouncing chords on the offbeat, fiddle carrying a fast reel-like riff, strummed steel-string acoustic guitar, melodic bass, live drums with a steady backbeat, tin whistle doubling the hook on the choruses. Bright live-in-the-room mix, light plate reverb. Male lead, bright and slightly nasal, clearly sung, with group backing voices on the choruses. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 142 BPM, A major. Wry, brisk, affectionate mood. No synthesizer, no distorted guitars, no autotune, no drum machine, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - fiddle, accordion and drums]

[Verse 1]
I wrote it on Tuesday, I fixed it on Wednesday
The minister's reading it now on the stage
I'm standing at the back by the fire-exit sign
Mouthing along to each page

[Pre-Chorus]
Here comes the pun, here comes the pun
Three lines, two lines, one

[Chorus]
And she skips it, she skips it
I mouth it at the back of the hall
Nobody's laughing, nobody knows
It was the best thing I wrote at all

[Verse 2]
The pigeon joke lands but the budget is long
She reads out the numbers too slowly
I'd cut that paragraph twice, I swear
She's lost her place, she's lost her place

[Pre-Chorus]
Here comes the end, here comes the end
She's looking up, she's looking up

[Chorus]
And she nails it, she nails it
The one that I thought would be cut
They're laughing, they're laughing
I'm grinning at the back, shut up

[Bridge - fiddle and accordion]
Nobody turns around to see me
That's the job, that's the job

[Chorus]
And she says it, she says it
In her voice, with my words on top
Nobody knows it, nobody knows
I mouth it at the back and I don't stop

[Outro - fiddle and accordion ring out]
